text.p: French electrical equipment group Schneider announced a 27 percent increase in first-half profits on Thursday and said it expected a marked rise in earnings for 1996 as a whole.
The company's shares dropped, however, with analysts saying the results came in at the lower end of expectations. The stock was down seven francs or 2.85 percent at 0830 GMT at 239 francs.
First-half net income rose 26.7 percent to 503 million francs ($97.4 million) from 397 million on the back of a rise in sales to 30.045 billion francs from 29.189 billion.
"The board of directors noted that the company achieved good results in the first half despite difficult business conditions in France and Germany," it said in a results statement.
"In light of recent activity trends, both in and outside France, Schneider can hope to see a very noticeable improvement in earnings for the full year."
Operating profit rose to 1.797 billion from 1.736 billion, while pre-tax profit from continuing operations increased to 1.450 billion from 1.198 billion.

The group said the rise in profit from continuing operations stemmed from a 15 percent increase in economic operating income -- which is operating income plus exchange rate gains or losses and rose to 1,884 million from 1,633 million -- and a decrease in the financial result.
Group sales rose 3.9 percent to 21.7 billion francs on a current structure and currency basis, or by 3.2 percent on a comparable basis of consolidation and exchange rates.
Sales fell 2.9 percent in France due to a downturn in industrial and construction spending. Europe sales rose 9.3 percent despite a slowdown in italy and a two percent fall in Germany, it said.
Sales in North America rose 5.7 percent, mainly due to sustained construction activity and Mexican recovery, it said.

Sales in the rest of the wolrd dropped 2.7 percent because of a drop in the number of contracts in some countries, which was offset in part by a strong rise in product sales in others, it said. ($1=5.164 French Franc)
